evidence.verdict: FIXTURE/INSTRUCTION ARTEFACT, not an arm effect. All 12 arm x checkpoint cells in the config-C grid are NO_MARKER: the v2 fixture declares no answer_marker, so grade_v3.py computed marker_required=False (grade_v3.py:404-406) and every row carries marker_lines=0 -- the ^ANSWER: rule was INERT for config-C and is not the cause of 0/3. The cause is a starved pinned working set: LR-01.v2.json pins resolve.py #L66-L110 (line 39 DEFAULT_MAX_REFS=64 is OUTSIDE the pinned range) and errors.py #L114-L126 (3 Ptr* classes, against expected 31), so cp.t12 and cp.t24 had no derivable answer from what the model saw. Cause 2 reinforces: cp.t24's own source pointer errors.py#L15-L142 contains 20 class definitions, never the expected 31 (= whole file, L15-L250). Cause 3: cp.t46's expected string mixes code with English 'before re-raising' and section 4 requires the anchor 'raising', so pointer-stable's substantively correct answer at rows-longrun-c-2026-10-26.jsonl:142 was graded missing_anchor:raising. The v2->v4 item diff proves the fixture authors repaired exactly the two starved pointers after config-C was recorded (resolve.py 1680->2785 B pointer #L66-L110 -> #L36-L110; errors.py 331->6353 B / 3 -> 31 classes pointer #L114-L126 -> #L15-L250; cp.t24 source L15-L142 -> L15-L250) and added the marker rule in the same revision, which is why v4 is the only grid where a checkpoint ever passed (pointer-stable cp.t12 'ANSWER: 64'). 0/3 licenses only: the four arms ran to N=48 and no arm scored a correct cp.t12/cp.t24/cp.t46 under LR-01.v2.json. It forbids any arm-quality comparison, any 'tie on quality' reading of clause (iii), any claim a checkpoint is unanswerable in principle, and any attribution of the zero to the marker. This does not contradict RUN-C-V2 frozen_rule_outcome verdict 'undecidable'; clause (iii) 'holds: true' remains vacuous, and this unit supplies the mechanism (the tie is at a broken instrument's floor, not a measured capability floor).
